ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On a clear and windless winter day, a child, along with a sled, starts from rest and slides down an inclined straight snow track with uniform acceleration. After traveling 54 meters, the sled enters a horizontal snow track, continuing for 40.5 meters before decelerating uniformly to a stop. The total mass of the child and the sled is 60 kg, and the entire sliding process takes 10.5 seconds. The inclination angle of the straight inclined track is 37 degrees (sin 37 degrees = 0.6).

1. Determine the magnitude of the maximum velocity $v_{\mathrm{m}}$ of Xiaoming and the ski sled during the sliding process.
2. Determine the time $t_{1}$ during which the child and sled were sliding on the inclined straight snow track.
3. Determine the magnitude of the average resistive force $F_{f}$ experienced by the child and sled on the inclined straight snow track.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a ski trail composed of two sections: on the right is a straight ski slope inclined upward, and on the left is a horizontal ski slope; the two sections meet at the bottom; in the figure, the child and the sled are near the horizontal section. From the image structure, it can be known that this is a two-section path in which the inclined-plane section and the horizontal section are connected; the sled first moves on the inclined-plane section to the junction, and then enters the horizontal section to move. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, the sled starts from rest and undergoes uniformly accelerated motion on the inclined straight ski trail, and after passing through the inclined-plane section distance s1=54 m, it reaches the junction; at this time the speed is maximum, denoted as v_m; afterward it undergoes uniformly decelerated motion on the horizontal ski trail, and after passing through the horizontal section distance s2=40.5 m, it stops. The total time is 10.5 s; let the time used on the inclined-plane section be t1, and the time used on the horizontal section be t2. The inclined-plane section is uniformly accelerated, the initial velocity is 0, the final velocity is v_m, and the average velocity is (0+v_m)/2, so: 54 = (v_m/2)t1. The horizontal section is uniformly decelerated, the initial velocity is v_m, the final velocity is 0, and the average velocity is (v_m+0)/2, so: 40.5 = (v_m/2)t2. Also there is the total time: t1+t2=10.5. From the first two equations, t1=108/v_m and t2=81/v_m are obtained. Substituting into the total time: 108/v_m + 81/v_m = 10.5, 189/v_m = 10.5, v_m = 18 m/s. Thus: t1 = 108/18 = 6 s, t2 = 81/18 = 4.5 s. The acceleration on the inclined-plane section: a1 = v_m/t1 = 18/6 = 3 m/s^2. Apply Newton's second law along the direction of the inclined plane; the component of gravity down along the inclined plane is mg sin37°, and the resistance F_f is upward along the inclined plane, therefore: mg sin37° - F_f = m a1. Take g≈10 m/s^2, m=60 kg, sin37°=0.6: 60×10×0.6 - F_f = 60×3, 360 - F_f = 180, F_f = 180 N.

40.5 = (v_m/2)t2.

189/v_m = 10.5,
v_m = 18 m/s.
Thus:

a1 = v_m/t1 = 18/6 = 3 m/s^2.

60×10×0.6 - F_f = 60×3,
360 - F_f = 180,
